subject: CAIQ claim acceptance & evidence gating — acceptance checklist and staging
messages:
From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@valerianhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: security@valerianhealth.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: CAIQ claim acceptance criteria + sample artifacts

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we prepare our internal sign-off, the security team asked for two things to close out the CAIQ review for the initial production scope: a short, actionable claim-acceptance checklist (so our reviewers know what artifact to expect for each answered control) and a small sample of runtime evidence demonstrating log retention and tenant separation for one week.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can provide a one-page acceptance checklist that maps each answered CAIQ claim to the exact artifact filename and owner?
- A downloadable sample (redacted) of runtime logs for a single tenant and the related crosswalk showing where the logs live in your platform?

We'd like to get the artifacts to legal and risk by EOD Tuesday (US Eastern). If there are any blockers — e.g., export scope or PII/redaction concerns — please flag those and the expected turnaround.

Appreciate it —
Laura Gomez
Senior InfoSec Manager | Valerian Health
laura.gomez@valerianhealth.com

Attachment: none

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@valerianhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ claim acceptance criteria + sample artifacts

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can definitely deliver a focused claim-acceptance checklist and a small, redacted runtime sample. High level plan and constraints below:

Plan (deliver by Tue EOD ET):
1) One-page claim acceptance checklist (XLSX + PDF) mapping CAIQ question -> claim -> expected artifact name -> Redwood owner. Will include a single-line acceptance criterion for each claim (e.g., "log retention verified via log-export manifest + sample tarball").
2) Runtime logs sample: a tarball with a single-tenant slice (containing sanitized request logs, tokenized IDs, and retention metadata) plus a minimal extraction manifest.
3) Annotated CAIQ crosswalk (PDF) showing which control families rely on the runtime logs versus platform config.

Constraints / notes:
- We will redact any user-identifiable content; extraction may remove message/text payloads and replace with stable hashes.
- Export will be scoped to one production tenant you designate; if you want a demo tenant instead, please confirm.
- For DocuSign/legal sign-off we can provide a short acceptance template (PDF) that your risk team can return.

I've looped in Marissa for evidence packaging and Priyom for the extraction run. Marissa — can you take point on assembling the checklist and annotated crosswalk? Priyom — can you confirm ETA for the runtime export and whether we need an internal ticket for PII redaction?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@valerianhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ claim acceptance criteria + sample artifacts

Stephanie / Laura —

Quick update on packaging. I prepared the initial checklist and crosswalk; attaching the working artifacts. Notes:

- Attached: "caiq-claim-acceptance-checklist.xlsx" — a compact sheet with three tabs: summary, claim->artifact mapping, owner roster. I filled in Redwood owners for each claim we previously asserted.
- Attached: "caiq-annotated-crosswalk.pdf" — visual overlay tying a subset of controls to runtime logging, key rotation, and tenant routing.
- Extraction: Priyom can run the extraction job; once complete I'll create a sanitized tarball named "runtime-logs-sample.tar.gz" and upload to the secure folder linked below.

Questions for Valerian:
1) Which tenant ID should we extract for the sample (prod-VAL-42 or a non-customer demo)?
2) Do you need the retention-policy timestamped manifest included in the tarball or as a separate CSV?

I'll keep the checklist intentionally terse so your reviewers can tick acceptance boxes. We can also produce a one-page "acceptance template" for DocuSign; draft attached as "docsign-customer-ack-template.pdf".

Priyom — if you can confirm the extraction window and redaction steps, I'll finalize the upload and send the secure link to Laura.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: caiq-claim-acceptance-checklist.xlsx, caiq-annotated-crosswalk.pdf, docsign-customer-ack-template.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@valerianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ claim acceptance criteria + sample artifacts

Marissa / team / Laura —

Confirming extraction plan and timeline:

- Scope: single tenant slice (prod-VAL-42) unless you request a demo tenant. Extraction will include request logs, KV cache meta entries, routing traces, and the retention manifest.
- Redaction: PII fields (user_email, full_text_payload) will be replaced with SHA256 hash placeholders; timestamps, event types, and routing attributes are preserved.
- Runtime export ETA: job scheduled to run tonight 23:00 PST; I expect the sanitized tarball available for upload by 03:00 PST tomorrow (Nov 30).
- Audit trail: I'll attach an extraction-run manifest and a small notes file describing redaction regexes applied.

Marissa — after I upload the tarball to the secure SharePoint folder, please confirm and notify Laura with the link.

On the acceptance criteria side, a couple of pragmatic suggestions for your checklist:
- Mark items as "Acceptable artifacts": Runtime tarball + manifest, Control owner attestation (email), Keystore rotation logs (for key-rotation claims), and DocuSign acknowledgement for final sign-off.
- For logging retention, include a sample of the log-retention lifecycle policy (policy id: retention-2025-ops).

I'll push the export now.

— Priyom
